subject: Throughput hedge & tail-latency carveout request — GreenCrest seasonal onboarding
messages:
From: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@greencrestlogistics.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Josh Bell <josh.bell@greencrestlogistics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput hedge / tail-latency carveout for holiday spike

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. Quick context: GreenCrest is moving a large portion of our anomaly-detection inference pipeline to Redwood Dedicated for Q4 (Oct–Dec). We have a committed reserved pool already (details in deal GC-2027-05) but our traffic model shows a 3x peak for short-lived routing events during weekly dispatch surges and an additional nightly batch that spikes GPU utilization for non-real-time workloads.

Risk: we’re worried the nightly batch jobs will trigger preemption/queueing that pushes up tail latency for our short inference calls (the ones powering routing decisions). For our use case the P99 tail during spikes is critical — even transient 500–800ms tails break SLOs downstream.

Ask: can Redwood provide a temporary throughput hedge and a tail-latency carveout for short RPCs during the Oct–Dec window? Specifically we’d like:
- A defined burst bucket (tokens or capacity) for seasonal spikes (estimate attached)
- Queueing rules that prefer short inference RPCs (<=200ms baseline) over nightly batch windows during defined carveout hours
- A short-term latency SLA (P99) for the short RPC tranche, or an explicit failover to a lower-capacity model variant that keeps latency bounded

Attached: GreenCrest_traffic_forecast.xlsx (traffic forecasts and example traces).

Would like to get a draft SLA addendum this week and a short call to align routing/observability hooks.

Thanks —
Sarah Ng
Product Ops, GreenCrest Logistics
+1 415-555-0123

---
Note: forwarded from Josh with sample perf traces attached for brevity.
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@greencrestlogistics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput hedge / tail-latency carveout for holiday spike

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the detailed forecast and the urgency. Short answer: yes, we can put together a bounded carveout and a temporary burst hedge for dedicated pools. We’ll need to agree on definitions (short RPC vs batch window) and the mechanics (burst tokens vs reserved carveout windows).

Proposed next steps (quick mutual action plan):
1) Redwood provides a draft SLA addendum that outlines: burst bucket size, carveout hours, queue priority rules, and P99 target for the short-RPC tranche.
2) GreenCrest confirms the traffic slices (attached forecast), which we’ll use to size the burst and carveout.
3) Technical sync: routing and cache pinning options — we’ll test pinning small hot KV keys to reduce tail variance.
4) Signing + onboarding timeline: target Oct 1 for policy rollout; DocuSign link to follow after internal approvals.

I’ve attached a first-pass draft (marcus_greencrest_sla_addendum_v0.1.pdf) — it’s intentionally conservative. Lauren, looping you for pricing and approval language.

Call options: I’m available Mon 09/13 10–12 PT or Tue 09/14 14–16 PT. Which works?

—Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0188

Attachment: marcus_greencrest_sla_addendum_v0.1.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 09:20:45 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Throughput hedge / tail-latency carveout — pricing impact

Looping Ben for pricing/contract language.

Marcus — quick notes from pre-review:
- We can structure the burst as a time-limited token bucket (Oct–Dec) sized to ~25% of committed throughput based on Sarah’s forecast.
- Offer: 10% credit on any overage above committed + burst usage during the season (to reduce sticker shock).
- Need confirmation from infra team on whether we can support "cache pinning" on dedicated pools (helps with P99 for hot RPCs).

Ben — can you run the numbers and flag whether the 25% seasonal bucket + 10% credit is acceptable? Also note: executive pricing sign-off required for >$200k season exposure.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 10:05:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Throughput hedge / tail-latency carveout — pricing impact

Thanks Lauren — quick calc attached.

Summary: the 25% seasonal burst bucket is workable but depends on two technical constraints:
1) Queue priority enforcement: we need a deterministic preemption/priority lane for short RPCs during carveout hours (we can implement via request class routing + tenant priority tokens). Without this, the bucket won't guarantee tail improvements.
2) Latency SLA scoping: we should confine any P99 SLA to the "short-RPC tranche" (payloads <X tokens and <50ms compute baseline). For long-running jobs we remain best-effort; propose the SLA explicitly exclude nightly batch windows if they exceed N concurrent nodes.

Pricing impact file: pricing_impact_greencrest_v2.xlsx (attached). If we move forward with 25% and 10% seasonal credit, expected incremental exposure is ~$78k for Oct–Dec (cashflow impact shown). Exec sign-off threshold noted.

If infra confirms queue priority + cache pinning, we can commit to a P99 target for the short tranche (we recommend P99 <= 180ms during carveout hours).

—Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: pricing_impact_greencrest_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@greencrestlogistics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Draft mutual action plan + updated SLA addendum (v0.2)

Sarah —

Thanks — we had an internal alignment meeting and here’s an updated, compact mutual action plan and timeline. I attached SLA_Addendum_GreenCrest_v0.2.pdf which reflects pricing notes and a routing approach:

Mutual Action Plan (short):
- Size: Burst bucket sized to ~25% of committed throughput for Oct 1–Dec 31 (per your forecast).
- Priority lanes: We will implement a short-RPC priority lane enforced in the serving runtime (request class with priority tokens).
- Latency SLA: Scoped to short-RPC tranche (payloads <512 tokens, service time baseline <50ms); provisional P99 target <=180ms during carveout hours. Noted exclusions: pre-existing maintenance windows and catastrophic failure modes.
- Cache pinning: Pilot pinning of top-50 keys on dedicated pool to reduce KV cold-starts.
- Overage: 10% seasonal credit on billed overage above committed throughput for Oct–Dec; internal pricing doc attached.
- Sign: DocuSign link will be sent once GreenCrest confirms stakeholders; aiming for signing by 09/20 so we can rollout Oct 1.

Proposed call: Wed 09/15 11:00 PT — Zoom link: https://zoom.redwood.ai/meet/greencrest-sync (please confirm). I’ll also open HubSpot task and send DocuSign. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/GC-2027-05.

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_GreenCrest_v0.2.pdf (pdf)

Let me know if the carveout hours need to be narrower.

—Marcus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@greencrestlogistics.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Josh Bell <josh.bell@greencrestlogistics.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft mutual action plan + updated SLA addendum (v0.2)

Marcus —

This looks good and aligns with legal/commercial expectations here. We’re prepared to sign the v0.2 addendum and proceed with the Oct 1 rollout. DocuSign route is fine — please send to legal@greencrestlogistics.com and ops@greencrestlogistics.com.

We accept the carveout scoping and P99 <=180ms for the short-RPC tranche as described. We’ll plan internal cutover on Oct 1 and a joint validation run the first week.

Attached: signed_cover_sheet.pdf (cover page to follow the DocuSign envelope).

Thanks for the quick turnaround — excited to get this live.

Best,
Sarah Ng
Product Ops, GreenCrest Logistics
